_comment: Data-driven intent classification rules for EU/ICAO phraseology. Loaded by src/atc/intent_rules.cpp. Schema: see intent_rules.hpp. Order of `rules` is priority order — first match wins. `normalize` patches Whisper transcription quirks before matching. `adjustments` apply post-match overrides (intent reassignment + confidence mutation) in array order.

normalize._note: Pilots say the frequency-change readback in the PRESENT PARTICIPLE about as often as the imperative -- 'contacting tower on 118.200' rather than 'contact tower ...'. Every READBACK pattern is written on the imperative ('contact ground/tower/approach/departure'), so the gerund matched nothing: confidence fell to 0.30, the LM was consulted and guessed READY_FOR_DEPARTURE_VFR, and the ground handoff guard -- which only exempts READBACK and LEAVING_FREQUENCY -- answered 'you are still on Ground, contact Tower on 118.200' to a perfectly correct readback (real vol LFLP 2026-08-14). The same pilot said 'Contact tower ...' on the two previous flights and was answered with silence, which is why this looked like a regression. Normalising the gerund fixes every 'contact X' pattern at once instead of doubling the rule table. [C. P. Potter]
Whisper drops the first 'r' in 'departure' (observed LSZB log 2026-06-07).
Whisper occasional slurred contraction of 'departure'.
Whisper sometimes drops one 'n' in 'runway'.
Voxtral drops the trailing 'e' from 'mode' in transponder readbacks (e.g. 'Mode Charlie' → 'Mod Charlie').
Voxtral substitutes 'more' for 'mode' in transponder readbacks (e.g. 'more Charlie' → 'mode Charlie').
Voxtral substitutes 'Pierre' (French first name) for 'clear' in takeoff readbacks (e.g. 'Pierre to take off' → 'clear to take off').
Same 'Pierre' substitution when Voxtral also drops the 'f' from 'off' (double error).
Same 'Pierre' substitution against the compounded 'takeoff' word.

Voxtral substitutes 'Pilgrim' for 'cleared' in landing readbacks: 'Pilgrim Land' for 'cleared to land' (LFMN ABDI8R 2026-07-13, caused a 'say again'). 'Pilgrim Land' is not ATC phraseology so global alias is safe.
Voxtral mishears 'Torino' as 'Tavino' when followed by a facility word (LIMF check-in). Scoped to the phrase so bare 'tavino' can never collide.
Torino → Tavino, tower variant.
Torino → Tavino, ground variant.
Torino → Tavino, radar/CTR variant.
Voxtral mishears 'Geneva' as 'Jimmy Van' (French-accented 'Genève' → 'Jimmy Van'). Fix: normalize globally. 'Jimmy Van' is not a real ATC term so safe to alias.
Voxtral mishears 'Marseille' as 'Massai' (French /maʁsɛj/ → 'Massai') in the Marseille Control handoff readback (LIMF→LFLP 2026-07-10). 'Massai' is not a real ATC facility so safe to alias globally.
Voxtral mishears 'France' as 'Franzen' on the France Control check-in (LIMF→LFLP 2026-07-10: 'Franzen, November...'). 'Franzen' is not a real ATC facility so safe to alias globally.
Voxtral mishears 'report established' as 'by Stabitch' — 'report' becomes 'by', 'established' becomes 'Stabitch'. Not a real ATC term so safe to alias.
Standalone Voxtral mishearing of 'established' as 'stabitch' (e.g. 'stabitch on final'). Not a real word so safe alias.
Voxtral substitutes 'heading' for 'holding' in the taxi/holding-point readback (e.g. 'heading point Alpha' → 'holding point Alpha'). 'Heading point' is not standard ATC phraseology.
Voxtral drops 'holding' and splits 'point' from what follows: 'a point to Alpha' for 'holding point Alpha'. 'A point to' is not standard ATC phraseology in the readback context — safe to alias.

Voxtral substitutes 'VFR' for 'verify' in the squawk verification readback (e.g. 'VFR squawk 3076' → 'verify squawk 3076'). Genuine VFR squawk readbacks say 'squawking VFR' or 'squawk 7000', never 'VFR squawk NNNN' with a specific code — the alias is unambiguous.

Voxtral occasionally hears the NATO letter 'Papa' as 'baba' (voiced b vs unvoiced p on plosive onset). 'Baba' is not standard aviation vocabulary and the mishearing is observed in callsign context ('X-Ray Baba') — global alias is safe. Static whisper_prompt already carries 'Papa' in the NATO list and every PTT bias carries the full callsign + trailing pair, so this normalize is defense-in-depth for the residual failures.

Voxtral language-model bias: when 'approved' appears earlier in the same PTT (e.g. 'startup approved, ... November X-Ray Papa'), the decoder can echo 'approved' where 'Papa' should be, yielding 'X-Ray approved'. 'X-Ray approved' is not a valid ATC phrase (approvals are on operations, not callsign letters), so the alias is unambiguous. Phrase-scoped — do NOT alias bare 'approved' which is a real ATC word.
Voxtral mishears 'Chambery' as 'Chamber' or 'Chambry'. Normalise to correct city name.
Voxtral drops the trailing 'y' from Chambery.
Voxtral mishears 'tower' as 'our' in frequency-change readbacks (e.g. 'contact our 118.200').
Voxtral mishears 'climbing to' as 'climb in to' (drops 'ing', adds 'in').
Voxtral mishears 'climbing to' as 'climb with' (drops 'ing', adds 'with').
Voxtral drops the 'Anne' prefix from 'Annecy' when followed by a facility word.
Voxtral drops the 'Anne' prefix from 'Annecy' when followed by ground.
Voxtral mishears 'decimal' as 'this symbol' in frequency readbacks (e.g. '118 this symbol 030' -> '118 decimal 030').

Voxtral drops the past-tense 'd' from 'established' before an approach type (RNAV/ILS). Fix so 'establish rnav' and 'establish ils' still match the text_contains:'established' guard in INITIAL_CALL_TOWER.
Same 'd'-drop fix for ILS establishment report.

Voxtral mishears 'direct' as 'director' in the direct-to readback ('Direct ROMAM, when able' -> 'Director Roman, when able', LFLP->LFMN 2026-08-07). 'Director' is not ATC vocabulary so the alias is safe; it also keeps the transcript log readable.
Voxtral SPLITS compound words. 'runway' comes back as 'one way' -- twice in the LSGG arrival of 2026-08-19 ('One way to 2' = 'runway two two'), which loses the runway from the readback entirely.
The same split with the first syllable intact.
'RNAV' is dictated letter-then-word and comes back split. Kept separate from the frequency hyphen handling, which already protects 'r-nav'.
Same, heard as the possessive.
Same, spelled out.

Voxtral turns 'decimal' into 'this is my' inside a frequency readback: 'Ground on 121, this is my 850' for 121.850 (LSGG 2026-08-20). No ICAO phraseology contains 'this is my', so the substitution is safe here.
Voxtral hears 'Rumble' for 'Romeo' in the callsign (real flight LSGG 2026-08-21). The callsign is the one word every rule keys on, so a mishearing there costs the whole transmission.
Readback of the landing clearance heard as one word, 'Pleatoland runway two-two' -- which drew a 'say again' on short final (LSGG 2026-08-21).
'Geneva Ground' called back as 'Grand' on the first taxi call (LSGG 2026-08-21). Anchored on the callsign that follows so the word 'grand' alone is never rewritten.

rules._note: Profanity / insults toward ATC. Highest priority so tone is caught even when other intent keywords are present.
Pilot-issued correction phraseology (rejecting ATC's interpretation). 'negative contact' / 'no contact' are EU traffic-advisory replies and must NOT be claimed here.
IFR clearance request to Delivery. Must come before REQUEST_TAXI / INITIAL_CALL_GROUND to prevent 'request taxi IFR' from being swallowed by the taxi rule.
Engine startup request — after IFR clearance readback, before taxi.

Pilot-initiated frequency change announcement (not a request, not ATC's own 'approved' readback). Either an unconditional sign-off phrase, OR a 'frequency change' phrase that is NOT a request and NOT ATC's approval ack.
Traffic-advisory replies must come BEFORE SELF_ANNOUNCE so 'traffic in sight' is not claimed by the CTAF announce rule.

IFR holding-point position report. Covers both bare 'holding point' (en-route to Tower) and the combined IFR departure call 'holding point runway X, ready for departure IFR to Y'. 'ready' is blocked only when 'ifr' is absent — this allows the full IFR pilot phraseology while still preventing VFR READY_FOR_DEPARTURE from matching here.

rules._note_direct_vector: IFR direct-to and vector readbacks ('direct ROMAM, when able', 'confirm direct ELMEM', 'turn left 247') used to match NO rule -> UNKNOWN -> routed to the LM, which guessed a check-in or a frequency request; that mis-guess stranded a flight with no controller for 17 minutes (LFLP->LFMN 2026-08-07). 'direct' is guarded against service REQUESTS and against the report-airborne check-in ('passing 3000, direct ROMAM' carries a facility word and/or 'passing' -> stays INITIAL_CALL_CENTER). The turn guard keeps VFR pattern calls ('turning left downwind/base/final') out, since READBACK is evaluated before the position-report rules. [C. P. Potter]
rules._note: Readback covers wilco/roger, frequency-change ack, sign-off phrases, control-zone clearances, taxi/clearance instruction echoes, takeoff/landing readbacks, VFR cross-country approvals, and transmissions ending in a runway-number token. 'holding point'/'hold short' only match when paired with a readback-context word (qnh/via/information) to avoid shadowing REPORT_HOLDING_SHORT. Explicit 'request' phrases (request taxi, request startup, request clearance) are excluded so a runway-token suffix does not swallow a service request. 'when ready' catches the frequency-handoff readback pattern ('Ground on 121.735, when ready') even when Voxtral/Whisper drops the word 'contact'. The compound none guard exempts 'contact'-prefixed phrases so 'contact ground on 121.735 when ready for departure' still fires READBACK even if 'departure' is present.

any._note: The PARTICIPLE plus a facility name is a sector CHECK-IN, not a readback: 'Milan Radar, November 750XP, climbing to flight level 210' is how a pilot reports in on a new frequency, and INITIAL_CALL_CENTER owns it. Excluded here rather than merely demoted, because READBACK is evaluated first and would otherwise win outright. [C. P. Potter]

rules._note_bare_freq: A frequency readback WITHOUT the word 'contact' -- 'ground on 121 decimal 850' -- matched nothing and fell to INITIAL_CALL_GROUND at 0.30, so Tower answered a perfectly correct readback with 'contact Ground' (real flight LSGG 2026-08-21; the user had already reported that saying 'contact' works and omitting it does not). Real pilots drop the verb. 'on 1' is the discriminator: every VHF frequency starts with a 1, so the pair <facility> + 'on 1' is a frequency readback and nothing else. [C. P. Potter]
rules._note_level_readback: A BARE LEVEL READBACK matched no rule at all: 'Climb flight level 110, November Romeo Charlie' scored UNKNOWN 0.00 and the whole thing rode on the cloud LM. On 2026-08-29 that LM answered HTTP 403 tier_not_allowed on every call, so the single most common IFR transmission drew 'say again, use standard phraseology' FIVE times in a row while the aircraft climbed correctly. The most frequent readback in IFR must not depend on a network round-trip. Guarded three ways: no service REQUEST, no REPORT ('passing'/'reaching' are reports, not readbacks), and the participle check-in form is demoted by an adjustment below when no readback is pending -- 'climbing to FL110' on a new frequency is a sector check-in and INITIAL_CALL_CENTER must keep it. [C. P. Potter]

rules._note: VFR cross-country departure: ready-for-departure plus a course/direction marker.
Parking/apron/etc. as the destination ('taxi to parking') — NOT pilot's location ('on parking, request taxi').

'clear of runway' / 'vacated runway' but NOT 'cleared for takeoff runway'. Whisper drops the second 'f' on 'take off' → 'take of', so guard against 'for take' (catches both spellings). 'left runway 14' counts as vacated, but 'left downwind' / 'left base' does not. 'clear...runway' with 'taxi' or 'squawk' in the same transmission is a taxi readback, not a vacated report.

any._note: PHRASE, not two loose words. 'all: [left, runway]' fired on every transmission naming a parallel runway: 'taxi to holding point Charlie One, runway zero four LEFT' was classified RUNWAY_VACATED at 0.90 on the ground at Nice, 2026-08-28. At any field with L/R runways that is EVERY taxi, line-up and landing readback. A genuine vacated report says 'vacated' and is caught by the first branch; this one only has to catch 'left the runway'. [C. P. Potter]

rules._note: Plain 'request taxi' but exclude frequency-change readbacks and taxi-instruction readbacks (which mention 'taxi' but are echoes, not requests). 'report ready taxi' is excluded because ATC says 'report when ready to taxi' and Voxtral may drop 'when'.
Position-Reports. 'report' (Tower-imperative) excluded so the pilot's readback of 'report downwind/final' is not misclassified as a position report.
Inbound/landing request, but only when no facility keyword (Tower/Approach) is present — those route to INITIAL_CALL_INBOUND/APPROACH instead.
US-specific VFR advisory service.

Calls to Approach Control or Departure Control. 'Radar' is NOT in this list — in real ATC 'XYZ Radar' is an en-route ACC/Center providing radar service (Milan Radar = Milan ACC), not a destination Approach controller. Matching 'radar' here would fire a destination approach clearance whenever the pilot check-ins with any en-route Center whose callsign includes 'radar', which is a routine phraseology. 'radar' is handled by the INITIAL_CALL_CENTER rule below.
rules._note_readback_guard: The descend-via/arrival READBACK carries the facility word inside its EXPECT clause ('descend via ABDIL 8R arrival ... expect RNAV Alpha approach runway 04L') and scored INITIAL_CALL_APPROACH 0.88 -> spurious bare 'radar contact' while the real readback stayed pending (LFLP->LFMN 2026-08-06). Clearance verbs below exclude those readbacks; the engine also reroutes a check-in intent with a pending readback + clearance verbs to READBACK.

rules._note: IFR en-route climb request. Pilot asks Centre for a higher FL. Guards against clearances ('climb FL190') and initial calls.
IFR en-route descent request. Pilot asks Centre to descend. Guards against readbacks ('descend FL110') and initial calls containing 'descend'.

En-route initial call to Area Control / UIR Centre / Radar. Facility words: 'control', 'centre'/'center', and 'radar' — 'XYZ Radar' is standard ICAO callsign for an ACC providing radar service (e.g. 'Milan Radar', 'Marseille Radar'). Fires before INITIAL_CALL_GROUND so 'Brest Control' doesn't accidentally match ground. Negative guards catch readbacks of handoff instructions ('contact Control on 119.755').

'contact ground' and 'when ready' indicate the pilot is reading back a frequency-handoff instruction ('contact Ground on 121.735 when ready'), not making an actual initial call to Ground. Voxtral sometimes drops 'contact', leaving 'Ground on 121.735 when ready' — 'when ready' guards that case.
Tower call with inbound/landing intent — beats INITIAL_CALL_TOWER below.

Pure initial contact only. If the transmission already carries a clear follow-up token (ready / request taxi/landing/touch / downwind / base / final / vacated / leaving / wilco / roger / going around), the specific rule above must win. Without this guard 'Bern Tower N172SP ready for departure' in TOWER_CONTACT was misclassified as a fresh initial call. 'contact tower' and 'when ready' guard against Voxtral dropping the word 'contact' in frequency-handoff readbacks.
Generic initial call — last resort if no specific facility variant matched. Mirrors the old match_initial_call() that delegated to ground OR tower.
Last-resort fallback for traffic-advisory replies. Single keyword 'looking' is ambiguous, so confidence is low and it appears at the very end of the rule list.

adjustments._note: Upgrade INITIAL_CALL_INBOUND → INITIAL_CALL_INBOUND_VRP when a VRP was named in the transcript (airport_vrps lookup populated msg.vrp_name).
Airborne intent while on ground — likely a readback of a clearance ('takeoff runway 06, report downwind'). Demote to READBACK at moderate confidence so the state machine treats it as such.
Ground intent while airborne — physically impossible. Demote confidence so the LM gets a chance to reclassify.
SELF_ANNOUNCE only makes sense on UNICOM at non-towered fields. At a towered airport the word 'traffic' is almost never a CTAF announcement.
Pilot called 'tower' at a non-towered airport — phraseology error. Lower confidence so the LM can correct the intent.
Post-landing 'request taxi' is a taxi-to-apron request, not a pre-departure clearance request. State machine has just seen LANDING_CLEARED (or TOUCH_AND_GO_CLEARED) within the just_landed window.

Defense in depth: an INITIAL_CALL_* intent only makes phraseological sense in the initial-contact window (IDLE / GROUND_CONTACT / TAXI_CLEARED — the latter to cover the tower_only auto-advance hop) OR when reporting established to Tower in IFR approach. Outside it (TOWER_CONTACT, PATTERN_ENTRY, LANDING_CLEARED, EN_ROUTE, ...) the matcher landed on the wrong rule; demote confidence so the LM can reclassify.

IFR approach tower: pilot says 'established [ILS/RNAV] [runway]' when checking in with Tower. 'established' in IFR/APPROACH_TOWER is unambiguously an initial Tower call — override regardless of whether 'tower' keyword was present.

IFR approach check-in with QNH: standard EUROCONTROL phraseology includes QNH in the initial call to Approach ('November 111RC, Melun Approach, descending 4500 feet, QNH 1025'). The READBACK rule matches 'qnh' at 0.90, shadowing INITIAL_CALL_APPROACH at 0.88. Promote only when (1) the text contains 'approach' (Approach facility keyword, as opposed to a plain descent readback), and (2) no readback is currently pending (readback_pending=false guards against a navlog step-down readback being misclassified). Note: has_facility is not a valid adjustment-rule key — use text_contains instead.

'climbing TO flight level 110' with nothing outstanding is a sector CHECK-IN -- so hand it to INITIAL_CALL_CENTER outright instead of merely demoting the confidence. Demoting sent it to the LM, and on 2026-08-29 the LM was returning 403 for every call, so the demotion turned a valid transmission into 'say again'. A transmission must always end somewhere: a readback (silence) or a check-in (ack), never in the gap between them. [C. P. Potter]
